attribution: Oded Gilad — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Lhagang (Tagong) Monastery, Kangding County, Garzê Prefecture, Sichuan
alt: Wide view of Tagong Monastery, a Tibetan Buddhist complex on the grassland of western Sichuan
caption: Lhagang Monastery at Tagong, about 3,700 m up on the grassland west of Kangding, a Sakya-order temple centred on a revered Buddha image. It is the first high point of the trip, and the altitude makes it the place where the group must go slowly.

attribution: Marym1718 — CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Zhonglu Tibetan Village, Danba County, Garzê Prefecture, Sichuan
alt: Stone Tibetan houses and fields of Zhonglu village on a slope in the Danba valley
caption: Zhonglu, one of the Gyalrong Tibetan hamlets of the Danba valley, with whitewashed stone houses on terraced slopes. It sits near 2,000 m, so after Tagong the group sleeps lower and can stay in a family guesthouse.

attribution: Munford — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Tall square stone watchtower rising above Tibetan houses in Danba
caption: A diaolou, one of the tall stone watchtowers that stand in the Gyalrong villages around Danba. Some date back several centuries, and walking among them is the main reason to spend a night here instead of driving straight back.

attribution: Shizhao — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Labrang Monastery, Xiahe, Gannan Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Gansu
alt: Monks and Tibetan pilgrims at Labrang Monastery in Xiahe
caption: Labrang Monastery at Xiahe, founded in 1709 and one of the six great Gelug monasteries, with pilgrims walking the kora circuit around it. It is a working monastery of several hundred monks; foreigners enter with a monastery guide and are asked not to photograph inside the halls.

attribution: Charlie fong — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Kumbum (Ta'er) Monastery, Huangzhong, near Xining, Qinghai
alt: Skyline of the golden-roofed halls and white stupas of Kumbum Monastery
caption: Kumbum (Ta'er) Monastery, birthplace of Tsongkhapa, founder of the Gelug school, 25 km from Xining. It is the one Xining-area site the French advisory names as open to foreigners, and the group reaches it from the airport on the day it flies in.

attribution: Ken Marshall from Taipei, Taiwan — CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Longwu (Lower Wutun) Monastery, Tongren (Rebgong), Huangnan Prefecture, Qinghai
alt: Whitewashed buildings and prayer wheels of Longwu Monastery at Tongren
caption: Longwu, the lower Wutun monastery in the Rebgong valley near Tongren, a centre of the thangka painting tradition. It breaks the Xining to Xiahe drive and shows the Amdo Tibetan culture that Labrang belongs to.

attribution: Terry Wu — CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Bands of red, orange and yellow sandstone hills in Zhangye Danxia
caption: The striped sandstone hills of Zhangye Danxia, formed by tilted Cretaceous red beds. Sunrise or sunset is when the colours show, and in March cold nights mean the walkways are quiet and the group can use the first shuttle.

attribution: Windmemories — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Gate tower of Jiayuguan Fort in the Gobi, with the Qilian Mountains behind
caption: Jiayuguan, the western end of the Ming Great Wall, a fortress built in 1372 where the Hexi Corridor narrows between the Qilian Mountains and the Gobi. The group spends one morning here before an afternoon train to Dunhuang.

attribution: Zhangzhugang — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Cliff face of the Mogao Caves with the rows of cave entrances and the nine-storey pavilion
caption: The cliff face of the Mogao Caves, a UNESCO World Heritage site holding about 490 decorated Buddhist caves cut between the 4th and 14th centuries. Entry is by timed, guided slots booked online in advance, which is the main planning constraint of the Dunhuang days.

commonsFile: File:Singing Sand Dunes and Crescent Lake (20230918100733).jpg
attribution: N509FZ — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Mingsha Shan and Crescent Lake, Dunhuang, Gansu
alt: Large sand dunes of Mingsha Shan with the small Crescent Lake and its pavilion at the foot
caption: The Singing Sand Dunes of Mingsha Shan with Crescent Lake at their foot, 6 km from Dunhuang. In March the dunes are cold and windy, but the lake stays open all year and the late-afternoon walk up the dune ridge is the closing outdoor moment.

commonsFile: File:Panda in Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding - 7708872342.jpg
attribution: George Lu — CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding, Chengdu, Sichuan
alt: Giant panda sitting among bamboo at the Chengdu research base
caption: A giant panda at the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding, north of the city centre. Pandas are most active at feeding time in the morning, so the group goes straight from the airport on the first day.

attribution: Jpatokal — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Chengdu double hot pot with a clear sour soup on one side and red chilli broth on the other
caption: A Chengdu double hot pot, with a mild pickled-vegetable broth beside the numbing red mala broth. It is the group's first night of Sichuan food, and a reminder that the city is a UNESCO City of Gastronomy.
